title: SSP-GNN: Learning to Track via Bilevel Optimization
abstract: arXiv:2407.04308v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: We propose a graph-based tracking formulation for multi-object tracking (MOT) where target detections contain kinematic information and re-identification features (attributes). Our method applies a successive shortest paths (SSP) algorithm to a tracking graph defined over a batch of frames. The edge costs in this tracking graph are computed via a message-passing network, a graph neural network (GNN) variant. The parameters of the GNN, and hence, the tracker, are learned end-to-end on a training set of example ground-truth tracks and detections. Specifically, learning takes the form of bilevel optimization guided by our novel loss function. We evaluate our algorithm on simulated scenarios to understand its sensitivity to scenario aspects and model hyperparameters. Across varied scenario complexities, our method compares favorably to a strong baseline.

translated_title: SSP-GNN：通过双层优化学习跟踪
translated_abstract: 我们提出了一种基于图的多目标跟踪（MOT）公式化方法，其中目标检测包含运动学信息和重识别特征（属性）。我们的方法将逐次最短路径（SSP）算法应用于在一批帧上定义的跟踪图。该跟踪图中的边代价通过消息传递网络（一种图神经网络（GNN）变体）来计算。GNN的参数（即跟踪器的参数）在包含真实轨迹和检测样本的训练集上进行端到端学习。具体而言，学习以双层优化的形式进行，并由我们提出的新型损失函数引导。我们在仿真场景上评估了该算法，以了解其对场景因素和模型超参数的敏感性。在各种不同的场景复杂度下，我们的方法与强大的基线相比表现更优。
tldr: 该论文提出SSP-GNN方法，将逐次最短路径算法与图神经网络结合用于多目标跟踪，并通过双层优化和新型损失函数实现跟踪器参数的端到端学习。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes SSP-GNN, which combines the successive shortest paths algorithm with a graph neural network for multi-object tracking, and learns the tracker parameters end-to-end via bilevel optimization guided by a novel loss function.
